scope: Python runtime modules under core plus public top-level facades
review_policy: The local quality suite enforces these limits; GitHub CI is disabled. Raising a limit requires an ADR or same-review architecture rationale. Revisit each runtime-line increase after removing comparable code.
runtime_line_budget_rationale: The 283-line increase centralizes descriptor-relative no-follow filesystem helpers, replaces duplicated artifact traversal, applies them to bounded chat file reads, stale-write checked atomic updates, no-overwrite creates, and private long-response artifacts so symlink swaps cannot redirect workspace writes or block reads on named pipes, rejects oversized voice files and stale per-chat transcriptions, redacts known credentials from Telegram network errors and tracebacks before logging, pins task undo deletion and ownership-record reads/updates to one opened root so a root symlink swap cannot redirect removal or metadata writes, and uses dual-clock deadlines so clock corrections cannot extend in-memory approvals and suspend time still expires them. Revisit after removing comparable runtime code. The 39-line increase secures SQLite databases and existing WAL/SHM sidecars with no-follow file descriptors before opening connections, and fails closed on permission or path-race errors. The 7-line increase ensures JobStore closes its SQLite connection when schema initialization fails. The 6-line increase makes bot shutdown attempt every resource close before surfacing the first failure. The 1-line increase resolves the database parent while preserving the final path component so JobStore rejects a pre-existing database symlink without changing its target. The 3-line increase keeps read-only job diagnostics on the requested database path and rejects symlinks before querying them. The 1-line increase applies the same final-component check to the persistent memory database so symlink targets are not chmodded or opened. The 22-line increase runs bounded acceptance commands in isolated POSIX process groups and terminates/reaps the group on timeout so descendants cannot continue changing the workspace. The 42-line increase caps captured acceptance stdout and stderr with the existing bounded stream reader while keeping error output useful and automated commands non-interactive. The 53-line increase propagates multi-agent cancellation through a thread-safe acceptance boundary and kills/reaps the POSIX command group instead of letting checks run until timeout. The 48-line increase registers acceptance process groups in the durable job store so startup recovery can terminate checks orphaned by an application crash. The 19-line increase adds descriptor-anchored os.fwalk deletion on Python 3.10, where shutil.rmtree lacks dir_fd, preserving scoped undo without following symlinks. The 9-line increase serializes previously unlocked MemoryStore reads and scope mutations on its shared SQLite connection, preventing concurrent callers from observing partial scope clears; revisit after equivalent query paths can be simplified. The 55-line increase tracks a delegated run before setup awaits, synchronously cancels active runs on SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGABRT before python-telegram-bot drains updates, and awaits process-tree cleanup before closing resources; it also refuses new agent runs during shutdown. Revisit after consolidating lifecycle tracking with the durable job owner. The 11-line increase displays worker expected outputs before approval and includes role, inputs, and outputs in risk detection so a second confirmation covers actions omitted from the top-level goal. The 19-line increase redacts secret-named environment values from every LightClaw log message and exception trace before console and JSONL handlers format records, closing leakage paths from otherwise unfiltered exception handlers. The 15-line increase creates JSONL log files with owner-only permissions, tightens existing files, rejects symlink and non-regular targets, and creates new log directories privately. The 6-line increase makes /clear revoke the current chat's unapproved and time-bounded actions and invalidates in-flight voice transcription so cleared requests cannot be approved later. The 11-line increase centralizes pending-action revocation so /clear scopes it to one chat and confirmed /wipe_memory clears it across chats while active runs remain untouched. The 8-line increase retries Telegram text sends once after a short rate limit and caps the wait at 30 seconds, preventing dropped user-facing results without holding handlers indefinitely. The 2-line increase centralizes one-shot cancellation across Telegram callbacks, signal shutdown, and worker heartbeats, so repeated requests cannot interrupt cleanup. The 1-line increase requires a second confirmation for filesystem move, copy, and replacement commands and correctly matches /etc/ system paths. The 28-line increase applies interaction age retention and the SQLite size ceiling to persisted summaries, discards derived summaries before source interactions under size pressure, and checkpoints after VACUUM to avoid deleting conversation records because of WAL bytes. The 9-line increase binds global memory-wipe confirmations to the initiating Telegram user and the existing dual-clock expiry helper, so shared group state and wall-clock changes cannot satisfy stale destructive confirmations. The 10-line increase keys in-memory summaries, active-summary guards, and invalidation generations by chat, Telegram user, and workspace so shared group chats cannot leak another user’s cached summary or suppress and restore it through concurrent summarization. The 43-line increase adds a byte-bounded, symlink-safe first-text-hunk diff preview in Telegram and trims file lists for phone review while preserving the complete patch attachment. The 19-line increase keeps the no-follow patch descriptor open across Telegram awaits, so replacing the artifact path after summary delivery cannot redirect the attached diff. The 13-line increase bounds the per-user summary cache to 128 least-recently-used entries and retains invalidation generations only while summaries are active, while SQLite remains the durable source. The 18-line increase bounds optional JSONL logging with 5 MiB rotation, three private backups, and 4,096-character free-form field caps, without adding dependencies. The 2-line increase attaches secret redaction to root and JSONL handlers so propagated provider and memory logs cannot bypass the filter. The 50-line increase finalizes abandoned multi-agent runs after orchestration exceptions by stopping workers and heartbeats, failing unfinished lanes, clearing active tracking, and notifying the chat. The 5-line increase rate limits paid voice transcription to six requests per Telegram user per minute before file download. The 3-line increase applies a per-user sliding-window limit to text-triggered model work and rejects excess requests before provider processing. The 9-line increase returns a clear Telegram recovery message when approved multi-agent setup fails before any worker starts; in-flight failures still use durable job finalization. The 58-line increase waits for multi-agent workspace, checkpoint, snapshot, and durable-job filesystem threads to finish across cancellation; a pre-job canceled run removes only its metadata-proven LightClaw workspace, while an existing job or announced workspace is preserved. The 6-line follow-up removes unannounced owned workspaces after ordinary preflight errors as well as cancellation. The 15-line net addition shares cancellation-safe task-workspace creation across single-agent and multi-agent setup, waiting for registration to finish and removing only the newly owned workspace if canceled. The 87-line addition carries the same cancellation guarantees through single-agent checkpoint and durable-job setup, waiting for background operations, canceling persisted lanes before agent launch, clearing active state, and preserving owned workspaces whenever a job record exists; shared workspace helpers keep single and multi setup consistent. The 18-line follow-up cancels durable jobs and clears active run tracking when SQLite or other setup failures occur after job creation but before agent launch. The 30-line follow-up retries one transient SQLite finalization failure and records terminal-state failure in the private receipt when persistence remains unavailable, so completed agent work is not silently lost. The 2-line follow-up logs and retries transient SQLite heartbeat errors so a background task cannot discard a completed run. The 5-line follow-up retries cancellation state writes once and preserves the owned workspace when active-run cancellation encounters a transient SQLite lock. The 3-line follow-up shares transient heartbeat recovery and durable cancellation between single-agent and multi-agent runs. The 7-line net reduction reuses the retrying durable cancellation helper for multi-agent stop handling. The 36-line follow-up shares retrying terminal job writes across single-agent and multi-agent runs and records failed persistence in the multi-agent receipt. The 7-line follow-up waits for the final workspace snapshot and cancels the durable job if the run is interrupted before finalization. The 31-line increase waits for the final snapshot, file-change scan, and patch generation before recording the single-agent terminal state, cancels durable jobs if any of those thread-backed phases is interrupted, marks patch-generation failures as failed jobs, and keeps CLI parsing available to direct execution-mixin consumers while moving that logic beside agent helpers. The 9-line follow-up rejects JSON or Markdown receipts over the existing byte ceiling before either private file is written, keeping writer output readable by the bounded receipt loader. The 11-line increase preserves one-shot task cancellation on Python 3.10, where asyncio.Task.cancelling is absent, while weak task references prevent repeated shutdown and callback cancellation from interrupting cleanup. The 8-line voice-review increase shows captions beside the transcript and rejects requests that cannot fit in one complete Telegram approval message. The 4-line follow-up reports the transcription provider HTTP status without response contents and distinguishes provider failure from a missing API key. The 48-line follow-up tracks active per-session chat requests so /clear can discard queued work and prevent an in-flight reply from restoring cleared history while allowing already-started work to finish. The 13-line follow-up shares the invalidation across `/wipe_memory`, serializes message registration during the global clear, and resumes new requests after the database clear completes. The 2-line follow-up reuses cancellation-safe thread completion for global memory wipes and discards summary caches before releasing chat admission, preventing cancellation from letting new messages race a still-running SQLite clear. The 7-line follow-up keeps cancellation-safe thread waits intact across repeated cancellation requests and reuses that helper during task workspace creation, preventing late filesystem side effects from outliving cleanup.
